study type: Retrospective review and prospective observational study
exposure: Time of day (10 p.m. to 6 a.m.)
outcome: In-hospital newborn fall (incidence, clinical characteristics, adverse outcomes)
Near miss events (incidence, characteristics, association with maternal factors)
cohort: Newborns who fell in the maternity ward (retrospective) and mothers in the postpartum clinic (<72 hours after delivery) and their newborns (prospective).
finding: In-hospital newborn falls occurred at an incidence of 1.8-2.4/10,000 live births, typically around 22 postnatal hours and during nighttime (10 p.m.-6 a.m.), without any known adverse outcomes for the neonates. Near miss events were experienced by 8.3% of mothers (44/1,000 days of postpartum hospitalization), predominantly in the first postpartum day and during nighttime, often associated with intense maternal fatigue and lack of companionship.
followup_time: Until hospital discharge (for falls) or within 72 hours postpartum (for near-miss events).
